questions.question: On a circle of radius 7 units, PQ and QR are chords of length 7 units each. What is the length of the chord PR in units?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the chord lengths (7 units) equal the radius (7 units), ΔPOQ and ΔQOR are equilateral triangles.

Thus, each chord subtends a 60° angle at the center, making the total central angle for chord PR = 60° + 60° = 120°.

Using the direct chord length formula: PR = 2 × R × sin(θ/2) = 2 × 7 × sin(60°).

PR = 14 × (√3 / 2) = 7√3 units.

To match the given options, multiply the numerator and denominator by √3: 7√3 × (√3 / √3) = 21/√3 units.

**∴ The correct answer is 21/√3 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the circle (R) = 7 units

Length of chords PQ = QR = 7 units

 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• O P Q R 
 
 60° 60° 7 7 7 7 PR = ? 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let O be the center of the circle. The radii OP, OQ, and OR all measure 7 units.

⇒ In ΔPOQ, we have OP = OQ = PQ = 7 units. Thus, ΔPOQ is an equilateral triangle, meaning ∠POQ = 60°.

⇒ Similarly, in ΔQOR, OQ = OR = QR = 7 units. Thus, ΔQOR is also an equilateral triangle, meaning ∠QOR = 60°.

⇒ The total central angle subtended by chord PR is ∠POR = ∠POQ + ∠QOR = 60° + 60° = 120°.

⇒ Applying the cosine rule in ΔPOR:

⇒ PR² = OP² + OR² − 2 × OP × OR × cos(120°)

⇒ PR² = 7² + 7² − 2 × 7 × 7 × (−1/2)

⇒ PR² = 49 + 49 + 49 = 147

⇒ PR = √147 = 7√3 units

⇒ To match the fraction format given in the options, multiply the numerator and denominator by √3:

⇒ PR = (7√3 × √3) ÷ √3 = 21/√3 units

**∴ The correct answer is 21/√3 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Central Angle Theorem for Chords

The length of a chord L in a circle of radius R subtending a central angle θ is directly given by the formula L = 2 × R × sin(θ/2).

Cosine Rule

In any triangle, the square of a side is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides minus twice their product multiplied by the cosine of the included angle: c² = a² + b² − 2ab × cos(C).

Equilateral Triangle Properties

When a chord length is perfectly equal to the radius of the circle, the triangle formed by the chord and the two radii is perfectly equilateral, with all internal angles naturally measuring 60°.

questions.question: In a circular race of 4800m, A and B start from the same point and at the same time with speeds of 36 km/h and 54 km/h. When will they meet again for the first time on the track if they are running in the opposite direction?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed in opposite direction = 36 + 54 = 90 km/h = 90 × (5/18) = 25 m/s.

Time to meet for the first time = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Time = 4800 ÷ 25 = 192 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 192 second.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the circular track = 4800 m

Speed of A = 36 km/h

Speed of B = 54 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/faa7231fc091da6e0b365ac3691a75486a52bee979089951a61b34bcded79ded.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = Speed of A + Speed of B

Time taken to meet = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

1 km/h = 5/18 m/s

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of A in m/s = 36 × (5/18) = 10 m/s

⇒ Speed of B in m/s = 54 × (5/18) = 15 m/s

⇒ Relative Speed = 10 + 15 = 25 m/s

⇒ Time to meet = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Time = 4800 ÷ 25

⇒ Time = 192 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 192 second.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting for the first time anywhere on the track

Time = Length of track ÷ Relative Speed. The relative speed is the sum of their speeds if moving in opposite directions, and difference of their speeds if moving in the same direction.

Meeting for the first time at the starting point

Time = LCM of individual times taken to complete one full round (LCM of T₁, T₂, ...). This applies irrespective of the direction of motion.

Speed Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s directly, multiply the given speed by 5/18. Conversely, to convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.
</p

questions.question: The average weight of 10 students is increased by half a kg when one of the students weighing 51 kg is replaced by a new student. Find the weight of the new student.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total increase in weight = Number of students × Increase in average weight

Total weight increase = 10 × 0.5 kg = 5 kg

Weight of new student = Weight of replaced student + Total weight increase

Weight of new student = 51 kg + 5 kg = 56 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 56 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial number of students = 10

Weight of the student replaced = 51 kg

Increase in average weight = 0.5 kg

**Formula Used:**

Average = Total Sum of Observations ÷ Number of Observations

 
 
 Group of 10 Students
 Average increases by 0.5 kg
 
 
 

 51 kg
 Leaves

 
 

 New Student
 Joins

 
 
 Net Weight Increase = 10 × 0.5 kg = +5 kg

**Calculations:**

Let the initial average weight of the 10 students be A kg.

⇒ Total initial weight of the 10 students = 10 × A = 10A

Let the weight of the new student be W kg.

When the 51 kg student is replaced by the new student W, the new total weight becomes:

⇒ New total weight = 10A − 51 + W

The new average weight increases by 0.5 kg, so it becomes A + 0.5 kg.

⇒ New average = (10A − 51 + W) ÷ 10

⇒ A + 0.5 = (10A − 51 + W) ÷ 10

⇒ 10 × (A + 0.5) = 10A − 51 + W

⇒ 10A + 5 = 10A − 51 + W

Subtracting 10A from both sides, we get:

⇒ 5 = W − 51

⇒ W = 51 + 5

⇒ W = 56 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 56 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Replacement Method in Averages

When a person is replaced by a new person, use the formula: New Value = Replaced Value + (Total Number of Items × Change in Average). If the average decreases, the sign before the change becomes negative.

Combined Average

When two groups of sizes n₁ and n₂ have averages A₁ and A₂ respectively, their combined average is given by: (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Inclusion & Exclusion Principle

If a new person joins a group and the average increases, their value is strictly greater than the old average. Conversely, if someone leaves the group and the average increases, their value was less than the old average.
</p

questions.question: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 6 hours and 8 hours, respectively. Both pipes are opened together for 3 hours. After that pipe A is closed, and B continues to fill the tank. In how many hours will the tank be filled?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity = LCM(6, 8) = 24 units.

Combined efficiency of A and B = (24 ÷ 6) + (24 ÷ 8) = 4 + 3 = 7 units/hr.

Work done in first 3 hours = 3 × 7 = 21 units, leaving 24 − 21 = 3 units.

Time taken by B to complete remaining 3 units = 3 ÷ 3 = 1 hour.

Total time taken = 3 (together) + 1 (B alone) = 4 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A to fill the tank = 6 hours

Time taken by Pipe B to fill the tank = 8 hours

Both pipes operate together for the first 3 hours.

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Time (hours)**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 6
 24
 4
 
 

 B
 8
 3
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Combined efficiency of A and B = 4 + 3 = 7 units/hr

⇒ Work completed in 3 hours = 7 × 3 = 21 units

⇒ Remaining work = 24 − 21 = 3 units

⇒ Time taken by B to complete the rest = 3 ÷ 3 = 1 hour

⇒ Total time required to fill the tank = 3 + 1 = 4 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 4 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Trick

Always assume Total Capacity as the LCM of the given times to avoid fractional calculations.

Efficiency Concept

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. Total Work = Efficiency × Time.

Emptying Pipes

If a pipe empties the tank, its efficiency is taken as negative during calculations.
</p

questions.question: Find the gain percentage, given that Siddhi sold her scooter for ₹71785 gaining (1)/(5) th of the selling price.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Selling Price (SP) be 5 units.

Given, Gain = 1/5 of SP ⇒ Gain = 1 unit.

Cost Price (CP) = SP − Gain = 5 − 1 = 4 units.

Gain % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100 = (1 ÷ 4) × 100 = 25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) of the scooter = ₹71785

Gain = 1/5 of the Selling Price

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = SP − Gain

Gain % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/33b55b8c1a584999d307faad8dbb4f7e559f1a8c219630e54e45ae78293a8b75.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Gain = (1 ÷ 5) × 71785 = ₹14357

⇒ CP = 71785 − 14357 = ₹57428

⇒ Gain % = (14357 ÷ 57428) × 100

⇒ Gain % = (1 ÷ 4) × 100 = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Base of Profit/Loss Calculation

Profit and Loss percentages are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless specifically stated to be calculated on the Selling Price.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always offered on the Marked Price (MP). Formula: Selling Price = Marked Price × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Successive Discount

If two successive discounts of x% and y% are given, the effective single discount is (x + y − xy ÷ 100)%.

questions.question: Find the value of (tan 55^circ)/(cot 35^circ)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If A + B = 90°, then tan A = cot B.

Here, the sum of the angles is 55° + 35° = 90°.

Therefore, we can directly say tan 55° = cot 35°.

Substituting this in the given expression, we get: cot 35° ÷ cot 35° = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: (tan 55°) / (cot 35°)

**Formula Used:**

cot(90° − θ) = tan θ

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let us change the denominator into terms of tangent to simplify the fraction.

⇒ We know that 35° can be written as (90° − 55°).

⇒ So, cot 35° = cot(90° − 55°)

⇒ Applying the complementary angle formula cot(90° − θ) = tan θ, we get:

⇒ cot 35° = tan 55°

⇒ Now, substitute this equivalent value back into the original fraction:

⇒ (tan 55°) / (cot 35°) = (tan 55°) / (tan 55°)

⇒ Both the numerator and the denominator are exactly the same, so they cancel out.

⇒ = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angle Identities

Two angles are complementary if their sum is 90°. Key conversion identities include: sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, sec(90° − θ) = cosec θ.

Reciprocal Identities

Trigonometric functions can be inverted to find their reciprocals: sin θ = 1 / cosec θ, cos θ = 1 / sec θ, tan θ = 1 / cot θ.

Pythagorean Identities

Important squared relations: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, and cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1.
</p

From the given data, find the ratio of the cost prices of a shirt and a trouser.

 
 

 Item
 Selling Price
 Profit
 
 
 
 

 Shirt
 ₹1,200
 20%
 
 

 Trouser
 ₹660
 10%
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price of Shirt = 1200 × (100 ÷ 120) = ₹1000

Cost Price of Trouser = 660 × (100 ÷ 110) = ₹600

Ratio of their Cost Prices = 1000 : 600 = 5 : 3

**∴ The correct answer is 5 : 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price of Shirt = ₹1,200 | Profit on Shirt = 20%

Selling Price of Trouser = ₹660 | Profit on Trouser = 10%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = [Selling Price × 100] ÷ [100 + Profit%]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/00157e377959601fa2ca4f34cdea9c6186e75b533abd0436a52000cf462ff9c4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP of Shirt = (1200 × 100) ÷ (100 + 20)

⇒ CP of Shirt = 120000 ÷ 120 = ₹1000

⇒ CP of Trouser = (660 × 100) ÷ (100 + 10)

⇒ CP of Trouser = 66000 ÷ 110 = ₹600

⇒ Ratio of CPs = CP of Shirt : CP of Trouser

⇒ Ratio = 1000 : 600

⇒ Ratio = 5 : 3

**∴ The correct answer is 5 : 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Formula

When an item is sold at a loss, the Cost Price is calculated as: CP = [SP × 100] ÷ [100 − Loss%]

Marked Price and Discount

The Selling Price is determined by subtracting the discount percentage from the Marked Price (MP): SP = MP × [100 − Discount%] ÷ 100

Ratio Simplification

A ratio a : b essentially represents the fraction a ÷ b. It is always expressed in its simplest equivalent form by cancelling the Highest Common Factor among the values.

questions.question: The mean proportional of 4a² and x is (1)/(5a) where a is a positive number, then the value of x is ____.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any continuous proportion, the square of the mean proportional is equal to the product of the first and third terms.

⇒ (1 / 5a)² = 4a² × x

⇒ 1 / 25a² = 4a² × x

⇒ x = 1 / 100a⁴

**∴ The correct answer is 1 / (100a⁴).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First term = 4a²

Mean proportional = 1 / (5a)

Third term = x

**Formula Used:**

Mean Proportional = √(First Term × Third Term)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5d6a0aa2ef30fd4ab8da488ae95ef28b9b3213da2b178ca53e33d7ab1dd99fd9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 1 / (5a) = √(4a² × x)

⇒ Squaring both sides, we get:

⇒ [1 / (5a)]² = 4a² × x

⇒ 1 / (25a²) = 4a² × x

⇒ x = 1 / (25a² × 4a²)

⇒ x = 1 / (100a⁴)

**∴ The correct answer is 1 / (100a⁴).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

For two given numbers a and b, the mean proportional x is calculated as x = √(a × b). It serves as the geometric mean between the two values in a continued proportion.

Third Proportional

For two numbers a and b, the third proportional c satisfies the continued proportion a : b :: b : c. It is calculated directly using the formula c = b² / a.

Fourth Proportional

For three distinct numbers a, b, and c, the fourth proportional d completes the standard proportion a : b :: c : d, yielding the formula d = (b × c) / a.

Compound Ratio

When two or more distinct ratios are multiplied together term by term (for example, a:b and c:d merge into ac:bd), the resulting combined ratio is known as a compound ratio.
</p

questions.question: After offering two successive discounts a toy with a marked price of ₹150 is sold at ₹105. If the value of the first discount is 12.5%, what is the value of the second discount?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Overall ratio of Marked Price to Selling Price = 150 : 105 = 10 : 7

First discount (12.5% = 1/8) ratio = 8 : 7

Second discount ratio = Overall ratio ÷ First discount ratio = (10 / 8) : (7 / 7) = 5/4 : 1 = 5 : 4

Discount value = 5 − 4 = 1 part reduction on a base of 5 parts.

Second discount percentage = (1 / 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹150

Final Selling Price (SP) = ₹105

First Discount (D₁) = 12.5%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b6fec68842b311a45e946229d516bceba8feb202041e8cc1f1e4990e377a09f9.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price = MP × (1 − D₁/100) × (1 − D₂/100)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Price after first discount = 150 − (12.5% of 150)

⇒ 12.5% in fraction = 1/8, so discount amount = 1/8 × 150 = ₹18.75

⇒ Price after first discount = 150 − 18.75 = ₹131.25

⇒ The second discount is given on ₹131.25 to make the final SP ₹105.

⇒ Value of second discount = 131.25 − 105 = ₹26.25

⇒ Second discount percentage = (26.25 / 131.25) × 100

⇒ D₂ = (1 / 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equivalent Single Discount

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the equivalent single discount is given by the formula: [a + b − (a × b) / 100]%.

Marked Price vs Cost Price

The direct relationship between Marked Price (MP) and Cost Price (CP) when profit and discount are given is: MP / CP = (100 + Profit%) / (100 − Discount%).

Buy X Get Y Free

When Y items are given free on the purchase of X items, the discount percentage is calculated on total items: Discount% = [Y / (X + Y)] × 100.

questions.question: The present ages (in years) of A and B are in the ratio of 3 : 4. Five years back, the ratio of their ages was 2 : 3. What is the present age (in years) of A?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of A and B (Present) = 3 : 4

Ratio of A and B (5 years ago) = 2 : 3

Notice that the difference between the present and past ratio parts is equal for both A (3 − 2 = 1) and B (4 − 3 = 1).

This 1 unit part corresponds to the age difference of 5 years.

Present age of A = 3 parts = 3 × 5 = 15 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Present ratio of ages of A and B = 3 : 4

Ratio of ages 5 years back = 2 : 3

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aa1a37ae114d77c7e62445a5e6e1fde813286ff6e2246c30c50fc9f78716c31e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the present ages of A and B be 3x and 4x respectively.

⇒ 5 years ago, age of A = 3x − 5

⇒ 5 years ago, age of B = 4x − 5

⇒ According to the question, the ratio 5 years ago was 2 : 3.

⇒ (3x − 5) / (4x − 5) = 2 / 3

⇒ By cross-multiplying, we get:

⇒ 3 × (3x − 5) = 2 × (4x − 5)

⇒ 9x − 15 = 8x − 10

⇒ 9x − 8x = 15 − 10

⇒ x = 5

⇒ Present age of A = 3x = 3 × 5 = 15 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The absolute difference between the ages of two persons remains constant throughout their lifetime. If A is 5 years older than B today, A will always be 5 years older than B, regardless of past or future scenarios.

Equalising Ratios for Age Problems

If the difference in the ratio parts of ages across two time periods is not equal for both persons, you can make them equal by multiplying the first ratio by the numerical difference of the second ratio, and vice versa.

Cross-Multiplication Method

For an initial ratio a:b, if both quantities change by exactly the same amount 'x' to form a new ratio c:d, then 1 unit part of the original ratio is given by x(c − d) ÷ (ad − bc).
</p

questions.question: Find the area (in cm²) of an equilateral triangle whose sides are 18 cm.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The area of an equilateral triangle can be computed directly using the square of its side length.

Area = (√3 ÷ 4) × a²

Area = (√3 ÷ 4) × 18 × 18

Area = 81√3

**∴ The correct answer is 81√3 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of the equilateral triangle (a) = 18 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of an equilateral triangle = (√3 ÷ 4) × a²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f54b878a90d10c52c649e52d493a43b8c5ef7a423f12c7c5436417678335338f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = (√3 ÷ 4) × 324

Altitude of an Equilateral Triangle

The height or altitude (h) bisects the base and divides the triangle into two equal right-angled triangles. Formula: h = (√3 ÷ 2) × a.

Inradius of an Equilateral Triangle

The radius (r) of the inscribed circle touches all three sides from the inside. Formula: r = a ÷ (2√3).

Circumradius of an Equilateral Triangle

The radius (R) of the circumscribed circle touches all three outer vertices. Formula: R = a ÷ √3.

questions.question: Find the remainder, if 19²⁰⁰ is divided by 20.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the negative remainder concept:

When 19 is divided by 20, the remainder is −1.

Therefore, when 19²⁰⁰ is divided by 20, the remainder will be (−1)²⁰⁰.

Since 200 is an even power, (−1)²⁰⁰ = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: 19²⁰⁰ ÷ 20

**Formula Used:**

By the Binomial Remainder Theorem, (x − a)ⁿ ÷ x leaves a remainder of (−a)ⁿ.

**Calculations:**

⇒ The given expression is 19²⁰⁰ ÷ 20.

⇒ We can rewrite the base 19 as (20 − 1).

⇒ So, the expression becomes (20 − 1)²⁰⁰ ÷ 20.

⇒ When expanded using the Binomial Theorem, all terms containing a multiple of 20 will be perfectly divisible by 20.

⇒ The only term left to determine the remainder is the last term: (−1)²⁰⁰.

⇒ Remainder = (−1)²⁰⁰

⇒ Since the exponent 200 is an even number, (−1)²⁰⁰ = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Binomial Remainder Theorem

When (ax + 1)ⁿ is divided by a, the remainder is always 1. When (ax − 1)ⁿ is divided by a, the remainder is 1 if n is even, and (a − 1) if n is odd.

Negative Remainder Concept

A negative remainder simplifies calculations. For example, 19 ÷ 20 gives a normal remainder of 19, but it can also be taken as −1 (since 19 is 1 less than 20). The final remainder must always be converted back to positive if it ends up negative.

Fermat's Little Theorem

If p is a prime number and a is an integer not divisible by p, then ap−¹ divided by p always leaves a remainder of 1.
</p

questions.question:
A total of ₹2,00,000 is divided into two parts for investing in different banks on simple interest. One yields 4% p.a. while the

other yields 6% p.a. If the total interest at the end of one year is equivalent to 4.7% p.a. on the whole amount, the amount (in

₹) invested in each bank is ________, respectively.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

By using the mixture and alligation rule directly on the interest rates:

Ratio of investments = (6% − 4.7%) : (4.7% − 4%) = 1.3 : 0.7 = 13 : 7

Total parts = 13 + 7 = 20 parts ≡ ₹2,00,000

Amount in 4% bank (13 parts) = (13 ÷ 20) × 2,00,000 = ₹1,30,000

Amount in 6% bank (7 parts) = (7 ÷ 20) × 2,00,000 = ₹70,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,30,000 and ₹70,000.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total principal = ₹2,00,000

Interest rate of Bank 1 = 4% p.a.

Interest rate of Bank 2 = 6% p.a.

Overall equivalent rate = 4.7% p.a. for 1 year

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5ccea50f1a263967c2a5efa52594c3a5bf6fa5704ac4a02a49ef7beb0c13f6fd.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total interest earned at 4.7% = (2,00,000 × 4.7 × 1) ÷ 100 = ₹9,400

⇒ Let the principal invested in Bank 1 be ₹x. Thus, the principal in Bank 2 will be ₹(2,00,000 − x).

⇒ Total Interest = Interest from Bank 1 + Interest from Bank 2

⇒ [(x × 4 × 1) ÷ 100] + [((2,00,000 − x) × 6 × 1) ÷ 100] = 9400

⇒ 4x + 12,00,000 − 6x = 9,40,000

⇒ 2x = 12,00,000 − 9,40,000

⇒ 2x = 2,60,000

⇒ x = ₹1,30,000

⇒ Investment in Bank 2 = 2,00,000 − 1,30,000 = ₹70,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,30,000 and ₹70,000.**

**__Additional Information__**

Mixtures and Alligations

It is an analytical method used to find the ratio in which two quantities must be mixed to obtain a desired average value. Rule: (Quantity of Cheaper) ÷ (Quantity of Dearer) = (Price of Dearer − Average Price) ÷ (Average Price − Price of Cheaper).

Simple Interest (SI)

It is the interest calculated only on the original principal amount. The principal remains constant throughout the tenure. Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Overall / Effective Interest Rate

When multiple investments are made at different interest rates, the overall interest rate is the weighted average of the individual rates based on the amount of capital invested in each scheme.

questions.question: Simplify (sin A)/(1 + cos A) + cotA, where A is an acute angle.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Put A = 30° in the given expression to quickly find the answer.

⇒ sin 30° / (1 + cos 30°) + cot 30°

⇒ (1 / 2) / (1 + √3 / 2) + √3

⇒ 1 / (2 + √3) + √3 = (2 − √3) + √3 = 2

Checking the given options for A = 30°, we get cosec 30° = 2.

**∴ The correct answer is cosec A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = sin A / (1 + cos A) + cot A

**Formula Used:**

⇒ cot A = cos A / sin A

⇒ sin² A + cos² A = 1

**Calculations:**

⇒ Expression = sin A / (1 + cos A) + (cos A / sin A)

⇒ Taking the LCM of the denominators:

⇒ Expression = [sin² A + cos A × (1 + cos A)] / [sin A × (1 + cos A)]

⇒ Expression = [sin² A + cos A + cos² A] / [sin A × (1 + cos A)]

⇒ Grouping the squared terms together:

⇒ Expression = [(sin² A + cos² A) + cos A] / [sin A × (1 + cos A)]

⇒ Expression = (1 + cos A) / [sin A × (1 + cos A)]

⇒ Expression = 1 / sin A

⇒ Expression = cosec A

**∴ The correct answer is cosec A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Trigonometric Identities

• sin² θ + cos² θ = 1
• 1 + tan² θ = sec² θ
• 1 + cot² θ = cosec² θ

Reciprocal Relations

• sin θ × cosec θ = 1
• cos θ × sec θ = 1
• tan θ × cot θ = 1

Half Angle Concept

The term sin A / (1 + cos A) directly simplifies to tan(A / 2). Understanding these relations can help save time during exam simplification problems.
</p

questions.question: If tanθ = (8)/(15), and θ is an acute angle, then the value of frac{sqrt{1 - sintheta}}{sqrt(1 + sintheta)} is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rationalize the given expression inside the square root:

⇒ √[(1 − sinθ) / (1 + sinθ)] = √[(1 − sinθ)² / (1 − sin²θ)]

⇒ (1 − sinθ) / cosθ = secθ − tanθ

Given tanθ = 8/15, from right-angled triplet (8, 15, 17), secθ = Hypotenuse / Base = 17/15.

⇒ secθ − tanθ = 17/15 − 8/15 = 9/15 = 3/5

**∴ The correct answer is 3/5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

tanθ = 8 / 15

We know that tanθ = Perpendicular (P) / Base (B)

Let P = 8 and B = 15.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a40183be6198e7269e123bf6ddab816b16c50934c6093cb6e52e0d8bf3993ca5.png] 

By Pythagoras Theorem:

⇒ Hypotenuse (H) = √(P² + B²)

⇒ H = √(8² + 15²) = √(64 + 225) = √289 = 17

⇒ sinθ = P / H = 8 / 17

**Evaluating the Expression:**

⇒ √(1 − sinθ) / √(1 + sinθ)

Substitute the value of sinθ:

⇒ √(1 − 8/17) / √(1 + 8/17)

⇒ √((17 − 8)/17) / √((17 + 8)/17)

⇒ √(9/17) / √(25/17)

⇒ √(9 / 25) = 3 / 5

**∴ The correct answer is 3/5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Triplets

Common right-angled triangle side ratios (P, B, H) include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25). Memorizing these saves calculation time in exams.

Basic Trigonometric Ratios

For a right-angled triangle: sinθ = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse, cosθ = Base / Hypotenuse, and tanθ = Perpendicular / Base.

Important Trigonometric Identities

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 | sec²θ − tan²θ = 1 | cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1
</p

questions.question: The radius of the base of a right circular cone is 9 cm and its slant height is 49 cm. Find the curved surface area of the cone.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The Curved Surface Area of a cone is given by πrl.

Since π contains 22 and r = 9, the answer must be a multiple of both 11 and 9.

Checking the options for divisibility by 9 (sum of digits must be a multiple of 9):

Only 1386 has a digit sum of 18 (1 + 3 + 8 + 6 = 18), which is perfectly divisible by 9.

**∴ The correct answer is 1386 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0f2f765e760f92db513aba94447d70699fddf90eeec5f49fa8037251e8db5edc.png] 

**Given:**

Radius of the base (r) = 9 cm

Slant height (l) = 49 cm

**Formula Used:**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a right circular cone = πrl

**Calculations:**

⇒ CSA = (22/7) × 9 × 49

⇒ CSA = 22 × 9 × 7

⇒ CSA = 198 × 7

⇒ CSA = 1386 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 1386 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of a Cone

The total surface area includes the curved surface area and the area of the circular base. Formula: TSA = πr(l + r).

Volume of a Cone

The volume represents the total capacity of the cone. Formula: V = (1/3)πr²h, where h is the perpendicular height of the cone.

Slant Height of a Cone

The slant height (l), radius (r), and height (h) form a right-angled triangle. Formula: l = √(r² + h²).
</p

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, the one who gets 88% of the votes is elected by a majority of 684 votes. What is the total number of votes polled? (all polled votes are valid)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Winner's vote share = 88%

Loser's vote share = 100% − 88% = 12%

Majority (Difference) = 88% − 12% = 76%

76% of total votes = 684

Total votes = (684 ÷ 76) × 100 = 900

**∴ The correct answer is 900 votes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Winning candidate's vote share = 88%

Majority (difference in votes) = 684

**Formula Used:**

Total Votes = 100%

Losing Candidate % = 100% − Winning Candidate %

Majority = Winning % − Losing %

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e863f1d6c5980e18f16c4a54d4ef4bbb4cef8fa378d2aaa8e8aebb568c71d178.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total number of polled votes be x.

⇒ Votes secured by the winning candidate = 0.88x

⇒ Votes secured by the losing candidate = x − 0.88x = 0.12x

⇒ Difference in their votes (Majority) = 0.88x − 0.12x = 0.76x

⇒ According to the problem, the majority is 684 votes.

⇒ 0.76x = 684

⇒ x = 684 ÷ 0.76

⇒ x = (684 × 100) ÷ 76

⇒ x = 9 × 100

⇒ x = 900

**∴ The correct answer is 900 votes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Valid and Invalid Votes

If some votes are declared invalid, then Valid Votes = Total Votes − Invalid Votes. The percentages of the winner and loser are typically calculated based on valid votes, unless specified otherwise.

Multiple Candidates Election

When there are more than two candidates, the majority is calculated as the difference between the votes of the winner and the runner-up (the candidate with the second-highest votes).

Percentage Base Method

Finding the total quantity when a part is given is a direct application of base percentage. Total Value = Given Value ÷ Percentage Fraction.

questions.question: In a ∆PQR, PQ = PR and PT is perpendicular to QR. If PQ = 17 cm, PT = 15 cm, then what is the measure (in cm) of QR?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In an isosceles triangle, the altitude drawn to the unequal side bisects the base.

This splits the triangle into two identical right-angled triangles.

Using the standard Pythagorean triplet (8, 15, 17), if the hypotenuse = 17 and perpendicular = 15, then the base (QT) = 8.

Since the altitude bisects the base, the total length of QR is twice the length of QT.

⇒ QR = 2 × 8 = 16 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ In ΔPQR, PQ = PR = 17 cm.

⇒ PT ⊥ QR and PT = 15 cm.

 
 
• 
 P Q R T 17 cm 17 cm 15 cm x x 

**Concept Used:**

⇒ The altitude drawn from the vertex of an isosceles triangle to its base exactly bisects the base.

⇒ ∴ QT = TR = QR ÷ 2.

**Calculation:**

⇒ In right-angled ΔPQT, apply Pythagoras theorem:

⇒ PQ² = PT² + QT²

⇒ 17² = 15² + QT²

⇒ 289 = 225 + QT²

⇒ QT² = 289 − 225 = 64

⇒ QT = √64 = 8 cm.

⇒ Since QT is exactly half of the base QR:

⇒ QR = 2 × QT

⇒ QR = 2 × 8 = 16 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Isosceles Triangles

In an isosceles triangle, the two angles opposite to the equal sides are also equal. Furthermore, the altitude drawn to the unequal side functions as an angle bisector and median simultaneously.

Pythagoras Theorem

Applicable only to right-angled triangles, it dictates that the square of the longest side (hypotenuse) equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides: a² + b² = c².

Common Pythagorean Triplets

Memorising frequent integer combinations dramatically reduces exam calculation time. Core examples include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), (7, 24, 25), and (9, 40, 41).

questions.question: If x + (1)/(x) = 2, then find the value of x²⁷²³ + (1)/(x³⁸³⁶⁾ = ?.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any algebraic equation of the form x + 1/x = 2, the value of x is always equal to 1.

Substitute x = 1 directly into the target expression.

⇒ x²⁷²³ + 1 / x³⁸³⁶

⇒ (1)²⁷²³ + 1 / (1)³⁸³⁶

⇒ 1 + 1 = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x + 1/x = 2

**Calculation:**

⇒ (x² + 1) / x = 2

⇒ x² + 1 = 2x

⇒ x² − 2x + 1 = 0

⇒ (x − 1)² = 0

⇒ x − 1 = 0

⇒ x = 1

Now, substitute x = 1 in the given expression:

⇒ x²⁷²³ + 1 / x³⁸³⁶

⇒ (1)²⁷²³ + 1 / (1)³⁸³⁶

⇒ 1 + 1/1

⇒ 1 + 1

⇒ 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity Case 1

If x + 1/x = −2, then the value of x is always −1. Here, x raised to any even power is 1, and x raised to any odd power is −1.

Algebraic Identity Case 2

If x + 1/x = 1, then x³ = −1. This is derived from multiplying the equation by x and using the sum of cubes formula.

Algebraic Identity Case 3

If x + 1/x = −1, then x³ = 1. This rule is extremely useful for reducing high powers of x by substituting x³ = 1.

Algebraic Identity Case 4

If x + 1/x = √3 or x² + 1/x² = 1, then x⁶ = −1.
</p

questions.question:
Simplify:

 ((7.3)³ - (4.7)³)/((7.3)² + 7.3 times 4.7 + (4.7)²)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The given expression is directly based on the standard algebraic identity for the difference of cubes.

Form: (a³ − b³) ÷ (a² + ab + b²) = a − b

Here, a = 7.3 and b = 4.7.

Result = 7.3 − 4.7 = 2.6

**∴ The correct answer is 2.6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: [ (7.3)³ − (4.7)³ ] ÷ [ (7.3)² + 7.3 × 4.7 + (4.7)² ]

**Formula Used:**

a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let a = 7.3 and b = 4.7

⇒ The given expression takes the form: (a³ − b³) ÷ (a² + ab + b²)

⇒ Substitute the formula for a³ − b³ into the numerator:

⇒ Expression = [ (a − b)(a² + ab + b²) ] ÷ (a² + ab + b²)

⇒ The common term (a² + ab + b²) in the numerator and denominator cancels out.

⇒ Expression = a − b

⇒ Expression = 7.3 − 4.7

⇒ Expression = 2.6

**∴ The correct answer is 2.6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Cubes Identity

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²). If the numerator has a '+' sign, the simplified result becomes (a + b).

Difference of Squares

a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b). This is extensively used to simplify fractional arithmetic expressions.

Perfect Square Identities

(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b².
</p

Given that marked price of a book is ₹270, what is the cost of paper to publish a single copy of the book if the marked price of a book is 20% more than its cost price?

Percentage cost of paper = 25% of the total cost price.

We are given that the marked price is 20% more than the cost price. This can be represented as:

 {MP} = {CP} times (1 + (20)/(100)) = {CP} times 1.20 

We can calculate the cost price (CP) from the given marked price (MP):

 {CP} = frac{{MP}}{1.20} 

**Calculations:**

Using the above formula, we find the cost price:

 {CP} = (270)/(1.20) = 225 

Next, we calculate the cost of paper, which is 25% of the cost price:

 {Cost of paper} = {CP} times (25)/(100) = 225 times 0.25 = 56.25 

**Conclusion:**

The cost of paper to publish a single copy of the book is ₹56.25.

If ₹42,000 were spent on Soccer, then the money spent on Badminton, Tennis and Rugby taken together is what percentage (rounded off to 2 decimal places) more/less than the money spent on Cricket, Swimming and Hockey taken together?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The degrees representing each sport in the pie chart are:

Soccer = 35°

Badminton = 45°

Tennis = 65°

Rugby = 25°

Cricket = 100°

Swimming = 60°

Hockey = 30°

₹42,000 were spent on Soccer, which corresponds to 35°.

We need to find the total expenditure and the percentage comparison of money spent on Badminton, Tennis, and Rugby versus Cricket, Swimming, and Hockey.

**Formula used:**

The total expenditure can be found by using the ratio of expenditure on Soccer (35°) to the total degrees (360°):

 (42,000)/(35) = (T)/(360) 

**Calculations:**

From the equation, we can find the total expenditure (T):

 T = (42,000 times 360)/(35) = 432,000 

So, the total expenditure is ₹432,000.

Now, let's calculate the money spent on Badminton, Tennis, and Rugby:

The degrees for Badminton, Tennis, and Rugby = 45° + 65° + 25° = 135°.

So, the money spent on these sports is:

 (135)/(360) times 432,000 = 162,000 

Thus, ₹162,000 is spent on Badminton, Tennis, and Rugby.

Next, we calculate the money spent on Cricket, Swimming, and Hockey:

The degrees for Cricket, Swimming, and Hockey = 100° + 60° + 30° = 190°.

So, the money spent on these sports is:

 (190)/(360) times 432,000 = 228,000 

Thus, ₹228,000 is spent on Cricket, Swimming, and Hockey.

Now, we need to find the percentage difference between the money spent on Badminton, Tennis, and Rugby and the money spent on Cricket, Swimming, and Hockey:

The percentage difference is given by:

 (162,000 - 228,000)/(228,000) times 100 = (-66,000)/(228,000) times 100 = -28.95\% 

**The money spent on Badminton, Tennis, and Rugby is 28.95% less than the money spent on Cricket, Swimming, and Hockey.**
